notes:
Background: Elmcrest EmbedShift is a mid-market SaaS that provides knowledge experiences for customer support and product docs. Currently using Postgres+pgvector for small customers and evaluating multi-tenant Pinecone for scale. Primary driver: reduce search latency while keeping embedding costs predictable as they scale.

Summary of fit: evaluating Redwood Hosted API first (fast onboarding) and then Dedicated reserved capacity for production traffic if POC meets throughput & cost targets. Heavy emphasis on embeddings throughput, nightly batch jobs (indexing 2M records/month), and connector/ingest flexibility.

Quoted requirements & constraints (from CTO Rita Lang & Head of Platform Daniel Cho):
- 95th percentile search query latency target: <100ms for semantic recall flows (with top-k rerank).
- Embedding throughput: need sustained batch embedding pipelines that can push ~100k embeddings/hour during nightly window and also support 200 qps streaming embedding for live features.
- Cost sensitivity: target <$120 per 1M embedding units (total cost to be compared hosted vs dedicated).
- Vector DBs: must integrate with Postgres+pgvector (current), test connector to Pinecone and ability to write vectors in bulk (ndarray upload).
- Data controls: SSO/SAML, per-customer data residency (US/EU), audit logging and KMS integration for keys.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2025-11-20: Inbound from product team, quick qualification call with AE Morgan (interested in embeddings/semantic search).
- 2026-01-19: Intro demo of Hosted API (basic embeddings + search demo). Positive reaction; asked for concrete throughput numbers.
- 2026-02-10: Security questionnaire submitted (requested SOC2, DPA, KMS details).
- 2026-02-27: Deep demo focused on batching, streaming embeddings, and Console dashboards. Recorded (Fireflies id ff_20260227_elmcrest_demo). CTO quote: "Need predictable P95 latency and predictable unit economics before committing reserved capacity."
- 2026-03-02: AE sent draft SOW for Dedicated POC and initial pricing ranges. Legal asked for SOC2 artifact (ticket SEC-1147).
- 2026-03-05: SE Jordan ran a technical call on vector ingestion patterns; Elmcrest to provide sample batches (1M vectors) and dataset schema.
- 2026-03-08: Internal budget committee flagged reserved capacity spend; working on cost comparison.

POC acceptance criteria (customer-proposed):
- Demonstrate ingest of 1M vectors in under 6 hours using Redwood pipeline + connector to their Postgres instance.
- Achieve 200 qps semantic search throughput at 95th percentile <120ms under production-like indexing.
- Provide cost projection for 12-month runrate comparing Hosted vs Dedicated (including reserved capacity discount scenarios).
- Verify SSO/SAML integration + KMS-encrypted keys + exportable audit logs.

Technical notes from SE:
- Elmcrest indexing pipeline prefers bulk HTTP endpoints for vectors; will test both Redwood direct write and connector flow.
- Batch windows are midnight-4am PST; prefer autoscaling burst for batch without affecting daytime P95 SLAs.
- Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations: automatic batching heuristics, cache suggestions for hot prefixes, and quantization profiles for CPU fallback.

Pricing/Commercial notes:
- Initial interest in 1-year reserved tier if POC proves throughput and cost within targets.
- AE provided ballpark: Dedicated monthly committed capacity estimate (GPU-hours) + hosted overage pricing. Elmcrest requested line-item quote by 2026-03-12.

Next steps (explicit):
- AE Morgan to finalize and send Dedicated POC SOW + performance test plan by 2026-03-11.
- SE Jordan to receive Elmcrest sample dataset (1M vectors) and confirm ingestion schema by 2026-03-13.
- Schedule 48-hour load window (target week of 2026-03-22) to run throughput tests with SE + infra on call.
- Legal to close SOC2/DPA questions; Redwood to provide report and KMS integration doc (ticket SEC-1147).

Open risks: legal clearance timeline, reserved capacity budget signoff, and potential connector work if their Postgres schema requires custom transformation.

Staging notes (sales shorthand):
